description: Broadcast-input multi-GEMM now requires scratch storage for every matrix rather than one input-sized scratch slice.
trigger: bszm_in=1, bszm_out>1, with A_had allocated only as large as A, as the retained interface comment describes.
expected_behavior: An input-sized scratch allocation should remain sufficient under the old contract, or the enlarged requirement should be documented and validated.
actual_behavior: The kernel now writes and reads A_had + j*size_m*size_k, including for broadcast A. Later matrices therefore address beyond an input-sized allocation. The wrapper does not validate scratch capacity. No repository Python construction site was found; external extension callers are the established interface boundary.

verification.description: Compared the prior conditional scratch-pointer advance with the new unconditional matrix-indexed offsets and inspected wrapper validation.
verification.limits: No external caller allocation or GPU memory violation was observed.
